design.concept: A calm two-step mobile surface. The first view is a compact list of team people, with a quiet name search on top, cards that show the name large with status and country behind it, and a create button that is always within thumb reach. Tapping a person, or the create button, opens the record view. It is a single column with name and country and a Save button pinned at the bottom. After a successful save it returns to the list with the person still marked.

views.purpose: Scan and search the team, spot the selected or just-saved person, load more people, and start a new registration.
One-field-per-line form to register a new person or correct the name and country of the selected one, with the save action pinned at the bottom and a way back.

design.decisions:
I followed the mobile section of the compactCrudTable template. The side panel becomes a scene of its own, switched only by the scenary host in mode=scenary with back. The list and the form never share a screen.

I chose the alternative groupviewtable--ml-responsive-table over the data table. The data table keeps three columns and scrolls sideways on narrow screens, which is forbidden on mobile. The responsive table turns each row into a labelled card.

The selected row is marked by the table's `value`, using the index of the selected person. After a save the person stays marked, and that is the success feedback. A success toast would be wiped by setScenario, which resets command results, so I dropped it.

The list has no total count, so I used a 'Ver mais pessoas' button that appends the next page instead of the pagination control. Paging stays wiring and is never a field.

Save is disabled while name or country is empty or while a request runs. Command errors show inline above the Save button, with contextual feedback, in the page body style. The scene title carries the person's identity when editing, and there is no extra page header.

The record view also shows the read-only status and contacts as a quiet definition list. The country is a text field because the contract offers no country list.

I did not add the unsaved-changes confirm on back. The host owns the back control, so the page cannot intercept it, and the drafts live in the shared state.

The empty, loading and error states are designed. A missing-precondition error says in words what is missing and offers a way back.
